repeating_paths.effect: ClaimApply transiently records wall/mono request samples. A non-lost refusal clears them before Idle; no snapshot/recovery phase exists to retain a future mono deadline. A lost refusal consumes a fresh persistent F key.

claim ID derives from fixed job index and current finite claim count. Every Claimed return consumes C; duplicate non-advancing fence aborts MonotoneFence instead of creating a state. Refusal creates no SQL attempt/reservation or new expiry.
only two booleans change. No counter, source write or time sample.

Requires adapter_reply.is_none(), then installs Some(AdapterReply). Cannot sample again until DriverReturn clears it while consuming a driver DAG edge. Interleavings may sample at different wall times, but do not overwrite a pending reply. The sample copies current wall and creates no future anchor; saved settlement creation consumes rank.
BIND_SQL changes only fixed resource/fence/job/node/boot/claim identity columns. No timestamp or counter/revision increment; full identity ranges over bounded captures.
first accepted release increments revision; repeats fail exact revision/expiry CAS. Release expiry is bounded above by an already captured expiry even when now advances.

latest selected capture equals current owned token whenever the same claim remains Running. Every RENEW_SQL guard needed for a Running resolver is shared; maximal revision cannot occur under bounded writes. Refused outcomes resolve to lost/settled/expired/cancel-requested or error/loss, never a fresh Running deadline. Successful renewal/resolution consumes N; CancelRequested bypasses deadline assignment.
production logical reads do not change durable rows. remember deduplicates exact returned tokens; claim/renew are the only selected creators of current Running token revisions.

original issue time is immutable; source deadline is issue+30000 and wake is min(current_mono+250,deadline), serviced only after reaching wake. At most120 wake assignments per consumed F key; terminal recovery clears phase and never slides deadline.
ordinary service and retirement inner phases are one-way; denied service does not resample a saved payload. Retirement samples copy current wall or -1 and do not create future anchors.

finite_valuation_argument.row_vocabularies: fixed Init literals/raw UUIDs plus bounded captures, finite source enums and arithmetic expressions over finite clocks/counters; all9 tables have bounded row counts above
finite_valuation_argument.episode_vocabularies: claims length2 values0..2; <=4 immutable claim snapshots; <=8 exact token captures; <=4 renewed IDs; <=3 lease captures; fixed boolean arrays; now from wall universe
finite_valuation_argument.worker_vocabularies: complete37-field raw Worker plus nested Ordinary/AdapterReply; finite source literal strings, fixed Init/claim IDs, finite capture indices and clock samples; no truncation/normalization
finite_valuation_argument.anchor_sets: sorted distinct subsets of finite wall-anchor [0,Wmax] and mono-anchor [0,Mmax] universes; retained vectors do not introduce values outside these source-derived universes
finite_valuation_argument.product_universe_formula: 7 * N_store * N_worker^2 * 2^2 * 2^2 * (Mmax+1) * 2^(Wmax+1) * 2^(Mmax+1) * 2^8; N_store and N_worker derive by finite field/row Cartesian products, not empirical cutoffs
finite_valuation_argument.not_termination: infinite stuttering/toggle/refusal/bind traces remain; only reachable valuations are finite
finite_valuation_argument.practical_limit: enormous cardinality bound does not prove fit, throughput, RSS, disk or largest-SCC feasibility
finite_valuation_argument.derived_raw_timestamps: non-anchor timestamps such as attempt.resolve_until=claim_time+120000 are bounded source expressions over finite clock values; they need not lie inside the visited-clock interval and remain exact
